correctness.rationale: Expanding the two potential-switch work contributions produces w=κDT Z²+κ X sqrt(2DT)Z. The conditional Gaussian mean and variance follow by Wick moments. The centered reward ξ=w−v(T+δ) has leading regularly varying product T(κDZ²−v) because the cross term has a moment strictly above q; this rigorously gives two positive signed c-tail coefficients. Classical i.i.d. stable, borderline-normal, and finite-variance attraction results then apply with the random renewal-count time change; backward renewal age is tight. The Gaussian cycle moments produce the finite-variance coefficient. A standalone 87-assertion checker verifies numerical formulas and inequalities only.

value.rationale: A directly motivated finite-duration harmonic trapping model has previously characterized Poisson work statistics, but does not explain energy-risk distributions under broad finite-mean non-Poisson clocks. This exact full three-regime law identifies a sharp q=2 fluctuation boundary and the unusual physical-clock-created negative heavy tail despite exponentially light negative raw work. The model-specific signed constants and monotone overhead response inform clock choice and asymptotic uncertainty without claiming a new general stable-limit theorem.
